reference: My pay's been delayed by the bank holiday — would Thursday be okay for the rent? Sorry about this.

reference: The flat's freezing because the old windows are draughty — any plans for double glazing?

verbose: The landlord has come inside the flat two times this month without telling us before, when we were not even at home, and this is making us very uncomfortable, so can you please speak to him about this matter once?
reference: The landlord's let himself in twice without notice — it's a bit much. Could you speak to him?

verbose: I am writing to inform you that the extractor fan in the bathroom is not working, so the steam is not going outside after taking shower, and the mirror and walls are getting wet and it is causing more and more mould everywhere.
reference: The bathroom extractor fan's broken, so the steam's causing more mould.

verbose: My flatmate is moving out next month, and I have already found one new person to take his room, so what is the process to change the names on the contract, and will there be any extra charges for doing that?
reference: My flatmate's leaving and I've found a replacement — how do we update the tenancy?

reference: The bedroom radiators are cold at the top — do they need bleeding? How do I do it?

verbose: There is some damp smell coming from the cupboard under the stairs, and when I opened it today, the walls were wet and some of our stored boxes are completely spoiled, so please come and check it when you are free.
reference: The cupboard under the stairs is damp and some boxes are ruined — could you take a look?

verbose: Is it possible that you can give us one more parking space for the second car, because we have only one allotted space and the street parking is always full in the evenings, so it is becoming very difficult for us daily.
reference: Is there any chance of a second parking bay? The street's always full in the evenings.

verbose: I wanted to check whether the rent includes the water and the internet bills also, or we have to pay separately for those things, because in the advertisement it was not very clearly mentioned anywhere, so I am confused.

verbose: The gutter on the roof is blocked with leaves, and whenever it rains, the water is overflowing and falling down the front wall, and now there is some damp patch coming inside the front room also, near the window.

verbose: Hi, just to inform you that the gas engineer came today for the yearly safety check, he has completed his work, and he said he will email you the certificate directly, so you should be getting it soon, nothing else is pending.
reference: Job done — the gas engineer's been and he'll email you the safety certificate.

verbose: Hi, sorry to disturb, actually I am your new neighbour from number twelve, we just moved in yesterday only, so I thought I will come and introduce myself and say hello to you properly, since we will be living next to each other.
reference: Hi, I'm your new neighbour at number twelve — we moved in yesterday. Just thought I'd say hello.

verbose: We are having a small birthday party for my son this Saturday evening in the garden, so there may be some noise till nine or ten o'clock, I just wanted to tell you beforehand only so that you don't mind it.

verbose: Your car is parked in front of my driveway since morning, and I need to go out urgently to take my mother to the hospital for her appointment, so can you please move it now, I am really in a big hurry.
reference: Sorry, your car's blocking my drive and I need to get Mum to hospital. Could you move it?

reference: Our cat's been missing two days — could you keep an eye out, and check your shed?

reference: Sorry, my son's kicked his ball into your garden — could he nip round and get it?

reference: Sorry, the foxes got into our bin bags — I'll clear up your side now.

reference: Your car alarm keeps going off at six and waking the baby — could you get it checked?

reference: We're away this weekend — could you put our bins out with yours? I owe you one.

reference: The storm knocked our shared fence down — shall we go halves on fixing it?

reference: Your son washed our car — lovely job, and ever so polite.

verbose: I accept your parcel deliveries happily, no problem at all, but your parcels are coming almost every single day now and sometimes I am not at home, so maybe you can choose some other safe place option on the website.

reference: Could you possibly watch the kids for twenty minutes while I nip to the chemist? My husband's poorly.

reference: The boiler bangs when the heating comes on and keeps losing pressure — can you service it?

verbose: Yes, I am ready to pay the extra amount, no problem at all, but please make sure that the work is done correctly this time, because I don't want to call you again and again for the same issue, it is very irritating.
reference: Fine, I'll pay the extra — just please make sure it's sorted this time.

verbose: Actually the kitchen sink is fully blocked, the water is not draining at all, and I already tried some chemical liquid from the shop, but nothing happened, so I think a professional is needed now, can you come?

reference: Could you explain "first fix" and "second fix" on the quote? I'm a little confused.

reference: The storm took some tiles off and the loft's leaking — could you patch it up today?

reference: We're after someone to mow and trim the hedges fortnightly — what do you charge?

reference: I've locked myself out — any chance you could come today? My wife's away till tomorrow.

reference: Thanks ever so much for coming out on a Sunday — the shower's perfect.

reference: I'm shopping around for quotes on the extension — nothing personal.

verbose: The light in the bathroom is flickering on and off since few days, and sometimes it is making some buzzing noise also, so I am a bit scared that it might be dangerous, can you please come and check it?
reference: The bathroom light's on the blink and buzzing — could you check it's safe?

reference: Nearly there — just a loose skirting board and a sticking door. When can you finish?

reference: Our boiler's fifteen years old — would a combi boiler suit a three-bed house?

reference: Are you running late? You said eight to twelve, and I've taken the day off.

verbose: Honestly speaking, if I were you, I would first of all call the electrician only, not the plumber, because the shower is the electric one, so the problem is most probably in the wiring and not in the pipes.
reference: I'd be inclined to ring an electrician first — it's an electric shower.

verbose: Yesterday at the party I accidentally told Sophie about the surprise trip her husband was planning for her birthday, I didn't know it was a secret, and now everybody is very angry with me, and her husband is not even talking to me properly.
reference: I let the cat out of the bag about Sophie's trip — I'm in the doghouse.
targets: let the cat out of the bag

verbose: My best friend is getting married next year, and he asked me to arrange the bachelor party, so I am thinking to take all the boys for one weekend to some city with good nightlife.
reference: I'm organising Tom's stag do — thinking a weekend away somewhere lively.

verbose: Oh my god, I am so tired, I have been running around the whole day doing shopping and cleaning and cooking for the party, I cannot even stand now, I just want to sit and sleep.
reference: I'm absolutely knackered — I've been on my feet all day.

verbose: Did you hear the news? Emma and her boyfriend have broken up after five years together, I just heard from her sister, I am very shocked, I thought they will definitely get married.
reference: Emma and her boyfriend have split up after five years — I'm gobsmacked.

verbose: I really wanted to get the tickets for that concert next month, but they got sold out within ten minutes, I was trying since morning, and I am feeling so sad and disappointed now.
reference: The concert sold out in ten minutes — I'm gutted.

verbose: I passed my driving test today on the first attempt only, I can't believe it, I was so nervous, but the examiner said I drove very well, and I am feeling so happy and proud of myself.
reference: I passed my driving test first time — I'm chuffed to bits!

verbose: I don't have any money left this month after paying the rent and all the bills, so I cannot come for the weekend trip, sorry, maybe next time when my salary comes I will definitely join.
reference: I'm skint till payday, so I'll sit this trip out — next time!

verbose: Okay, let me tell you about my date last night, it was really good actually, we talked for hours and he was very funny and kind, and we have decided to meet again next week also.
reference: Last night's date went really well — we're meeting up again next week.

verbose: My sister's family is coming to stay with us for the whole Christmas week, three adults and three small children, so our small house will be totally full, there will be no space to move even.
reference: My sister's lot are staying over Christmas — there'll be no room to swing a cat.
targets: no room to swing a cat

verbose: My parents are coming for Sunday lunch this week, so I am thinking to make the full roast chicken with potatoes and vegetables and gravy, the proper traditional British way, like they like it.
reference: My parents are coming for Sunday lunch, so I'm doing a proper roast.

verbose: Should we do something on Friday night? I am getting bored sitting at home every weekend, so I want to go out and have some fun, maybe go dancing or something like that, what do you think?
reference: Let's go out on Friday and let our hair down — I'm going stir-crazy.

verbose: You know that guy who is working at the café near my house, he is very friendly and very helpful always, he remembers everyone's order, he is a really good and nice person.
reference: The bloke at my local café is lovely — remembers everyone's order.

verbose: I am not able to understand why my brother is always arguing with me at family functions, every time he says something irritating, and then the whole evening is spoiled for everyone.
reference: My brother always winds me up at family dos and ruins the evening.

verbose: Did you see the match last night? Our team lost very badly, five-nil, I could not believe it, I was so angry, I switched off the TV in the second half itself.
reference: Five-nil last night — I was fuming and switched off at half-time.

verbose: Can I stay at your place tonight? I missed the last train and I don't have money for a taxi, so I will sleep on the sofa only, and I will leave early in the morning, I promise.
reference: I've missed the last train — could I kip on your sofa?

verbose: I am going to the shop now to buy some things for dinner, so do you need anything from there, like milk or bread or something, because I can bring it for you also on my way back.
reference: I'm nipping to the shops — need anything?

verbose: Actually I invited you for dinner, so please don't pay, I will pay the full bill today, and you can pay next time when we meet, it is my treat for your promotion, seriously.
reference: Put your money away — my shout. Congrats on the promotion!

verbose: Did you see what Jack posted online? I mean, he is always showing off his new car and holidays and expensive watches, it is too much, I don't like that type of behaviour at all.
reference: Jack's always blowing his own trumpet online.

verbose: She is always complaining about everything, the weather, her job, her husband, everything, and I cannot listen to it anymore, because every time we meet, she is complaining continuously.
reference: She's forever having a moan about something.

verbose: Bro, the movie we watched yesterday was totally boring and stupid, the story was very weak, and the acting was also very bad, I really wasted my money and time on that one.
reference: That film last night was absolute pants.

verbose: Do you remember we used to go to that small café near the college every day? I was in that area yesterday and I saw it is still there, same owner, same menu, it brought back so many memories.
reference: I walked past our old college café yesterday — not been in for donkey's years.

verbose: I am so sorry that I forgot your birthday yesterday, I was very busy with work and completely lost track of the dates, so please don't be angry, I will take you out for dinner to make up.
reference: So sorry I forgot your birthday — let me make up for it with dinner.

verbose: Are you coming to the barbecue on Sunday? Everybody is bringing something, so maybe you can bring some drinks or a salad or dessert, whatever is easy for you to bring, no pressure.
reference: Coming to the barbecue on Sunday? Bring a bottle or a salad.

verbose: She was looking so beautiful at the wedding, honestly, the dress, the hair, the makeup, everything was perfect, and everybody was looking at her only throughout the whole function.
reference: She looked stunning at the wedding — dressed to the nines.

verbose: My husband is having just a small cold, nothing serious, but he is lying in bed the whole day and acting like he is very seriously ill, you know how men are, so dramatic.
reference: He's got a sniffle and he's acting like it's the end — classic man flu.

verbose: Hey, how are you doing? Long time no see, what is going on in your life these days, everything good, how is the job and the family, tell me everything properly, I want to know.
reference: Hiya! Long time no see — how's it going?

verbose: Yes, yes, definitely I will come with you for the cinema and dinner, I am totally free tonight, so please include me in the plan and tell me the time and place where I should meet you all.
reference: Count me in — what time and where?

verbose: Last night I was telling you something important, but you were not listening at all, you were looking at your phone the whole time, it was very rude, honestly, I felt very bad.
reference: You were glued to your phone all night — I was a bit miffed.

verbose: We should all meet up properly one of these days, it has been so long, and everybody is so busy, so let us fix a date now only, otherwise it will never happen, as usual.
reference: Let's pencil in a date now, or it'll never happen.

verbose: Honestly my flatmate is so irritating these days, she leaves dirty dishes everywhere and plays music loudly late at night, and she never cleans the bathroom, I am really getting frustrated.
reference: My flatmate's doing my head in — dishes everywhere, music till all hours.

verbose: My grandmother is turning ninety next month, so the whole family is planning one big party for her, all the cousins are coming from different cities, and it will be a very big celebration.
reference: Nan turns ninety next month — the whole family's throwing her a big knees-up.

verbose: Yesterday I was walking in the market and suddenly I met my old school friend whom I have not seen for fifteen years, it was such a surprise, we went for coffee and talked for hours.
reference: I bumped into an old school mate after fifteen years — we chatted for hours.

verbose: I want to join the gym, but before that I want to know the monthly fees, and whether there is any joining fee extra, and also can I cancel anytime or there is some fixed contract period?
reference: What's the monthly fee, and is there a notice period if I cancel?

verbose: Basically I want to freeze my gym membership for two months because I am going abroad for work, so I don't want to pay for those months when I am not using it, is that possible for you?
reference: Can I freeze my membership for two months while I'm abroad?

verbose: I have not been to the gym for almost six months now, I have become very lazy, but from next Monday onwards I am definitely going to start again and also eat only healthy food.
reference: Six months without the gym — I'm turning over a new leaf on Monday.

verbose: Excuse me, are you using this machine, or can I use it now? Because I see your towel on it, but you are sitting there on the phone since fifteen minutes, so I thought I will ask.
reference: Do you mind if I jump on this? You've been on your phone a while.

verbose: I want to join one local running group, something friendly for beginners, where people run together on the weekends, not very serious or competitive, just for fun and fitness and meeting people.
reference: I'm after a friendly beginners' run — maybe parkrun?

verbose: The personal trainer is making me do so many exercises that my whole body is paining since two days, I cannot even climb the stairs properly, it is too much, honestly speaking.
reference: I'm completely worn out — my trainer's had me aching for two days.

verbose: Our five-a-side football team needs one more player for the Thursday evening matches, because one guy has injured his ankle, so are you interested, it is very casual only, nothing serious?
reference: Our five-a-side team's a player short — are you up for it?

verbose: The changing room showers are always cold in the evenings, and the lockers are also broken, so for this much monthly fee, I think the facilities should be much better than this.
reference: Cold showers and broken lockers — not great for the price.

verbose: Honestly, I am thinking to join the book club in the library, but I am a little bit worried that everyone will be very intelligent and I will not be able to speak anything clever about the books.
reference: I fancy the library book club, but I'd feel like a fish out of water.
targets: like a fish out of water

verbose: Can I bring one friend with me to the gym for one day only, just to try, because she is thinking about joining, so is there any guest pass or free trial day available for her?
reference: Is it alright if I bring a friend for a trial session?

verbose: We have the tennis club annual dinner next month, and they are asking everyone to wear formal clothes, like suit and tie for men and long dress for ladies, it is very fancy.
reference: The tennis club dinner next month is black tie.

verbose: I am the treasurer of our local cricket club, and the membership fees have not been paid by many members this year, so I have to remind them again and again, it is very tiring.
reference: As club treasurer, I'm forever chasing up unpaid subs.

verbose: I have been going to the gym regularly for three months, but I am not seeing any difference in my body or weight, so I am thinking maybe I should change my routine or diet.
reference: Three months of gym and no change — back to the drawing board.

verbose: I heard there is one drama group in the village hall, so do they take anybody, or there is some audition first, because I acted in college long back, but nothing after that, so I am rusty.
reference: Does the village am-dram group audition? I've not acted since college.

verbose: The swimming lessons for my son at the leisure centre are full for this term, so is there any waiting list where I can put his name, or should I check again next term?
reference: The leisure centre swimming lessons are full — is there a waiting list?

verbose: I am not able to come for the badminton practice tonight, sorry, because I am feeling very weak and tired, I think I have caught some viral fever, so I will stay at home and rest.
reference: Sorry, I'll miss badminton tonight — I'm feeling under the weather.

verbose: Our walking group is going on a long hike in the Peak District this Sunday, about fifteen miles, so if you are interested to come, wear proper shoes and bring a raincoat and lunch.
reference: Fifteen miles in the Peaks on Sunday — bring boots, a cagoule and lunch.

verbose: I was trying to cancel my gym membership online, but the website is not allowing me, they are saying I have to come in person and fill one form, it is very complicated just for cancelling.
reference: Cancelling my gym's a palaver — I have to go in and fill in a form.

verbose: Shall we play one game of tennis this Saturday morning in the park? I have not played since a long time, so I will be very rusty, please don't laugh if I play very badly.
reference: Are you up for tennis on Saturday? I'm rusty, so go easy.

verbose: Excuse me, there is one man who is not wiping the machines after using them, and he is leaving sweat everywhere, it is very unhygienic, so can you please remind him about the rules?
reference: Sorry to be a pain, but someone's not wiping down the machines.

verbose: The football club is selling tickets for the full season for all home matches, it is much cheaper than buying each match ticket separately, so I am thinking to buy for me and my son.
reference: I'm thinking of season tickets for me and my son — much cheaper.

verbose: My knee is paining a bit after the running yesterday, so should I still do the leg exercises today, or should I rest for some days first, what do you suggest as a trainer?
reference: My knee's a bit sore after yesterday's run — should I skip legs today?

verbose: My daughter wants to join the children's choir at the community centre, the one with the concerts and uniforms and all, so do you know how to sign up and whether there is a long waiting list in this area?
reference: Lucy's keen to join the children's choir — is there a long waiting list?

verbose: Hey, are you coming to the pub after the match on Saturday like usual? All the team members are going, and it will be fun, last time we stayed till very late, remember?
reference: Coming to the pub after the match on Saturday? The whole team's going.

verbose: At the gym today one man was showing off lifting heavy weights and making loud noises, everybody was looking at him, honestly, he was making a big show of himself for nothing.
reference: Some bloke at the gym was showing off — all mouth and no trousers.

verbose: Hello, I got a message saying my parcel was delivered today afternoon, but I have been at home the whole day and nobody came to the door, and I cannot find the parcel anywhere outside.
reference: My parcel's marked as delivered, but I've been in all day and there's nothing.

verbose: The delivery man left a card saying he tried to deliver but nobody was at home, but actually I was at home only, he did not even ring the bell, he just put the card in the letterbox.
reference: He's put a card through the letterbox without even knocking — I was in.

verbose: Can you please leave the parcel with my neighbour at number fourteen if I am not at home, or else you can keep it behind the bin in the side garden, it will be safe there.
reference: If I'm out, please leave it with number fourteen or behind the wheelie bin.

verbose: I ordered the groceries online for delivery between six and seven in the evening, but it is already eight now and nobody has come, and nobody is picking up the phone in customer care.
reference: Is my shopping running late? It was due at six and no one's answering.

verbose: The box arrived today, but when I opened it, the glass vase inside was completely broken into pieces, and the packing was very poor, so I want a replacement or a refund immediately.
reference: The vase arrived in pieces — the packaging was rubbish. Replacement or refund, please.

verbose: Hi, I am the delivery driver, I have one parcel for your neighbour who is not at home, so can you please accept it on her behalf and give it to her when she comes back in the evening?
reference: Would you mind taking a parcel in for next door?

verbose: Actually, the parcel needs a signature, and I will not be at home tomorrow because of office, so can I collect it from the depot instead, or can you deliver it on Saturday?
reference: It's recorded delivery and I'm out tomorrow — can I collect from the depot?

verbose: The courier has thrown my parcel over the gate into the garden, and it has been raining since morning, so now the box is completely wet and the books inside are also spoiled, so I am really very upset about this.
reference: My parcel was left in the front garden in the rain — the books are ruined.

verbose: I want to know the exact time of the delivery tomorrow, because the website is showing only between eight in the morning and six in the evening, and I cannot stay at home whole day waiting.
reference: Any chance you could narrow down tomorrow's slot? I can't wait in all day.

verbose: I need to return this item, so do I have to print the label at home and go to the post office, or will some courier person come and collect it from my house directly?
reference: Do I drop off the return at the post office, or will a courier collect?

verbose: We ordered the food one hour ago, and the app is showing that the driver is still at the restaurant, so we are very hungry now, can you please check what is happening with our order?
reference: We ordered an hour ago and the driver's still at the restaurant — what's the hold-up?

verbose: The order came, but they have missed one item, the garlic naan is not there, and also they have sent chicken curry instead of lamb, so the order is totally wrong, and I want a refund.
reference: The order was shambolic — no garlic naan, and chicken instead of lamb.

verbose: The furniture people are coming to deliver the wardrobe tomorrow, but our flat is on the third floor and the building has no lift, so please inform them to bring two people to carry it.
reference: We're third floor, no lift — they'll need two people for the wardrobe.

verbose: Can you please not ring the doorbell when you come, because my baby will be sleeping at that time, so just knock softly or send me a message, and I will come down and collect it.
reference: Please don't ring the bell — the baby's asleep. Just text me.

verbose: I keep missing my parcels because I am at work in the daytime, so is there any option that I can get them delivered to a pickup point or locker near the station instead of home?
reference: I'm never in by day — could I pick up parcels from a station locker?

verbose: The milkman has stopped delivering milk to our house from last week without giving any information, and we have paid for the whole month in advance, so what happened, why is he not coming?
reference: We've paid for the month, but the milk's stopped turning up.

verbose: Thank you so much for carrying the heavy boxes all the way up to the fourth floor, I know there is no lift and it was very difficult for you, I really appreciate your effort, thank you.
reference: Thanks so much for lugging those up four flights — much appreciated.

verbose: I don't feel like cooking tonight, I am very tired, so let us just order something from outside, maybe Indian or Chinese or pizza, whatever you feel like eating, I am fine with anything.
reference: Can't be bothered to cook — shall we get a takeaway? I'm easy.

verbose: Your app says that the delivery was handed to resident, but I live alone and I was not even at home, so who signed for it, and where is my parcel now, this is a very serious matter.
reference: It says "handed to resident", but I live alone and was out — I smell a rat.

verbose: The supermarket delivery has replaced the items I ordered with some other brands which I don't like, without asking me, so I want to reject these substitutions and get the money back.
reference: I won't be fobbed off with substitutions — I'd like a refund.

verbose: I want to send this parcel to my brother in Birmingham, and it is very important documents inside, so I want some proof that it is delivered and that he has signed for it.
reference: Recorded delivery to Birmingham, please — it's important paperwork.

verbose: How much is one stamp for sending a normal letter, but I want it to reach tomorrow itself if possible, not the slow one, because it is a birthday card for my mother.
reference: A first-class stamp, please — it's a birthday card for Mum.

verbose: I want to send this small packet to India, it has some sweets and clothes for my family, so how much will it cost and how many days it will take to reach there approximately?
reference: How much to post this parcel to India, and how long will it take?

verbose: Where is the nearest post box from here? Because I have one letter to post and I don't want to stand in this long queue just for one letter, it will take half an hour.
reference: Where's the nearest postbox? I don't want to queue for one letter.

verbose: I received a card that my parcel is waiting at the post office because I was not at home, so I have brought the card and my ID, can you please give me my parcel?
reference: There you go — my card and ID. I've a parcel to collect.

verbose: Can I renew my car tax and pay my bills here at the post office, or only letters and parcels, because my friend told me that they do many other services also these days?
reference: Can I pay road tax here, or is it just post?

verbose: I need to withdraw some cash from my bank account here, because the cash machine outside is not working, and the bank branch in our town has closed down permanently last year.
reference: The cash machine outside's broken — can I withdraw cash here?

verbose: Is the post office open on Sunday also, or only Saturday half day, because I am working full week and I can come only on weekends, so I wanted to confirm the timings once.
reference: What are your weekend opening hours? I work all week.

verbose: Please wait, I have to stick these stamps on all the envelopes, there are thirty wedding invitations, so it will take some time, you can serve the next person in the meantime.
reference: Thirty invitations to stamp — do serve the next person while I crack on.

verbose: I sent a parcel two weeks back to my friend in Scotland, but still she has not received it, and the tracking is also not updating since many days, so can you please find out where it is?
reference: A parcel I sent to Scotland a fortnight ago hasn't arrived. Could you look into it?

verbose: Sorry, I am a little bit confused, which form I have to fill for sending this parcel abroad, the customs form, and do I need to write the value of each item separately also?
reference: Which customs form do I fill in for abroad? Do I list each item?

verbose: The queue in the post office was so long today, there were only two counters open and twenty people waiting, and I stood there for forty-five minutes just to post one parcel.
reference: Forty-five minutes in the post office queue — with two counters open!

verbose: Hello, I want to redirect all my post from my old address to my new address for some months, because I have moved house and some letters are still going to the old house.
reference: I've moved house — can I set up mail redirection from my old address?

verbose: Do you sell those padded envelopes and boxes here, because I want to send one small fragile item, and I don't have proper packing material at home, so I want to buy some.
reference: Do you sell padded envelopes? I need to post something fragile.
